name: Fermented beverages, non-tea
anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
native_basis_label: ready-to-drink liquid, as consumed (wet weight, single strength); a concentrate or a powder-to-liquid product is assessed as reconstituted to single strength per the manufacturer's own directions, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 write into their juice cells and Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 writes into its beverage entries
scope_note: Ready-to-drink fermented non-dairy beverages whose ferment substrate is not tea: water kefir, kvass, fermented juice and vegetable drinks, drinking vinegars and shrubs, switchel, tepache, and low- and no-alcohol fermented fruit and grain beverages. Wine, cider, perry and beer are OUT of this row's scope and are not certifiable under it; they are held in development. The reason is stated plainly because it is a limitation and not a boundary of convenience: the only credible-set lead value this register carries for any of those four forms is the Hong Kong Cap 132V Wine cell (hk_cap132v_pb_wine_200), and the EU 2023/915 wine, cider, perry and fruit-wine lead cells are absent from the register. Selecting a strictest applicable value out of a pool that is known to be missing an instrument is not an execution of the government-limit-only method, so no ceiling is published for those forms. The absence is logged as a register gap; when those cells are ingested through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway the row is recompiled and the four forms are admitted against the strictest applicable value rather than against the residue of an incomplete pool. Dairy kefir and other cultured dairy drinks route to Category 24; kombucha and any tea-substrate ferment route to the kombucha row; a fermented drink carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16. The row's distinctive hazard is process rather than agronomic: fermentation drives the matrix to pH 2.5 to 3.8 and holds it there for days to weeks in contact with vessels, seals, taps and tubing, which makes equipment leaching a first-order route for lead, nickel and chromium, and that is why the lot-testing and escalation obligations in the control cells are written around equipment and not only around ingredients.
basis_guard: as[ _]consumed|wet weight|reconstituted|ready.to.drink|product as placed on market|\bjuice\b|single-strength|bottled water|portion ordinarily consumed
basis_guard_note: This row publishes a ready-to-drink liquid ceiling, so every named anchor must itself be written in a wet as-consumed (or as-placed-on-market liquid, or packaged-drinking-water) basis. The guard refuses any dry-commodity as-sold cell, any feed-basis cell, any food-contact migration limit and any article-content limit, because applying a dry leaf, bean or powder maximum level to a brewed or reconstituted liquid would be exactly the basis conflation Method v2.0 forbids. No brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented in either direction.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.basis: as consumed, ready-to-drink fermented beverage (read across from the Hong Kong wine cell)
Pb.label: No credible sovereign has written a lead maximum level for a non-tea fermented beverage as a class. Hong Kong Cap 132V's Wine cell (200 ug/kg, as consumed) is the only credible sovereign lead value this register carries for any fermented beverage, and it is adopted by disclosed read-across as the row ceiling for the non-alcoholic and low-alcohol ferments in scope. Wine itself is not certifiable under this row; see the scope note.

Pb.substantiation: The candidate set and the rejections, stated plainly because this is the cell most open to attack. The audit scan flags the entire juice and nectar lead family as stricter and unselected: the EU and Codex fruit-juice cells (30 ug/kg), the Hong Kong grape-juice cell (40 ug/kg), the EU and Hong Kong berry and small-fruit juice cells (50 ug/kg) and the US FDA Juice HACCP hazard-control level (50 ug/kg). All were considered and all are rejected on the same two grounds: a finished ferment is not a fruit juice, a juice from concentrate or a nectar within those instruments' scope, and fermentation is precisely the step that changes the matrix and opens the equipment-leaching route, so an unfermented-input cell does not describe the certified product. The packaged-drinking-water standards (5 to 10 ug/kg) govern water sold as water. That leaves the Wine cell, which is a genuine sovereign value for a fermented fruit beverage in the identical as-consumed basis. HMTc adopts it for the ferments this row certifies and does not conceal two things about it. It is weak: because the acid ferment sits against equipment for weeks, this cell carries mandatory lot testing with an equipment and closure investigation on any result above 30 ug/kg, and it is a declared Standards Ratchet priority under Governance Policy section 12. And it is drawn from a pool the register is known to be missing entries from: the EU 2023/915 wine, cider, perry and fruit-wine lead cells are not in the register, their absence is logged as a register gap, and it is filled neither by an occurrence value nor by recollection of the instrument. That gap is why wine, cider, perry and beer are excluded from this row's scope rather than certified against 200 ug/kg, and it also qualifies this read-across for the forms that remain: if any of the missing cells is stricter than 200 ug/kg it becomes the nearest applicable sovereign value for a fermented beverage and supersedes this anchor at the next recompilation. Until then the read-across is published with that qualification on its face rather than as a settled ceiling.

Cd.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for a non-tea fermented beverage. No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for wine, cider, beer or any other fermented beverage; the only cadmium values for fermented drinks anywhere in the register are non-credible-tier wine cells (MERCOSUR and Paraguay at 10 ug/kg), which sit outside the credible-regulator set and were not used. The absence of a credible cadmium cell for fermented beverages is reported as a regulatory gap. No near-neighbour read-across is supportable, so the fail-safe disposition is a control: cadmium testing is mandatory on every certified lot and no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
Cd.reference_method: Cadmium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result above 10 ug/kg in a ready-to-drink form, or above 100 ug/kg in a dry form, escalates to an ingredient-origin and process-water investigation and is a Standards Ratchet surveillance input under Governance Policy section 12.

tAs.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for a non-tea fermented beverage. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg) and write unspeciated arsenic limits only in the packaged-water and public-water-supply schedules, which are Category 8 instruments. The inorganic-arsenic cell in this row carries the health-relevant fraction. Total arsenic is therefore mandatory on every lot as the parent screen and no total-arsenic ceiling is invented.
tAs.reference_method: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, or 20 ug/kg where this row publishes no inorganic-arsenic number. Species never substitute for the total: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement.

iAs.basis: wet weight, ready-to-drink beverage (read across from the EU fruit-juice inorganic-arsenic cell)
iAs.source_scope: fruit juices, concentrated fruit juices as reconstituted, and fruit nectars
iAs.label: No credible sovereign has written an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for a fermented beverage. The EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit-juice cell (20 ug/kg) is the strictest sovereign inorganic-arsenic value for any ready-to-drink beverage and is adopted by disclosed read-across in the identical liquid basis.
iAs.substantiation: Beverage-to-beverage read-across with no basis change, adopted in the strict direction. Unlike lead, arsenic has no equipment-leaching route that fermentation opens up: it arrives with the water, the fruit or grain substrate and any added mineral salts, and an aqueous beverage cell at 20 ug/kg describes that route. Non-credible-tier fermented-beverage arsenic cells (MERCOSUR and Paraguay wine at 200 ug/kg total arsenic) are far looser and outside the credible set.

tHg.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-mercury maximum level for a non-tea fermented beverage. The sovereign mercury values in this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 total mercury at 2 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, written for inorganic mercury at 6 ug/kg) and the fish and seafood methylmercury and total-mercury ceilings, none of which governs this product form. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in this supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel, so testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
tHg.reference_method: Total mercury by ICP-MS (or dedicated amalgamation AAS) on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A detection above 5 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient and process-water investigation and reflexes methylmercury speciation.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a non-tea fermented beverage: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

Ni.basis: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink beverage (read across from the EU beverage nickel cell)
Ni.label: No credible sovereign has written a nickel maximum level for a fermented beverage. EU 2024/1987's fruit and vegetable juices and nectars cell (250 ug/kg) is the only sovereign nickel value written for a ready-to-drink beverage and is adopted by disclosed read-across in the identical liquid basis.
Ni.substantiation: Beverage-to-beverage read-across with no basis change. Nickel matters more in this row than in an unfermented beverage because a low-pH ferment held for weeks against stainless vessels, welds, taps and tubing is a live leaching condition, so the control obligation is written around equipment qualification and not only around ingredients. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte and a declared Standards Ratchet surveillance priority for this row.

Sn.basis: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid (inorganic tin)
Sn.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5.2 sets inorganic tin in canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, at 100 mg/kg = 100000 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V sets canned beverages at 150000 ug/kg. The EU value is the strictest applicable and binds. This is a direct sovereign maximum level on the beverage-in-a-can form, not a read-across.
Sn.substantiation: Tin in a beverage is a tinplate and can-lining migration pathway, so the government instruments are written on the canned form and the canned form is where the hazard sits. The EU cell (100000 ug/kg) directly governs every canned or tinplate-packaged product in this row and is adopted as the row ceiling for all packaging formats; a carton, PET, glass or pouch format has no tin source and complies trivially, so no separate non-canned cell is published. The looser Hong Kong canned-beverage cell (150000) and the canned-foods cells for solid foods (EU 200000; Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong 250000) are disclosed and deliberately not adopted: EU writes a stricter cell specifically for beverages and HMTc preserves that product-form split. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte; an elevated result in a non-canned format is a packaging-integrity signal.

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for a non-tea fermented beverage. The only sovereign aluminium values in a dietary basis are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 secondary allowable level 200 ug/kg, EU 2020/2184, Health Canada 2900 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the FSANZ infant-formula aluminium limits, which are Category 1 and are excluded from this category's anchor set by the taxonomy boundary rule. In this form aluminium is a packaging and processing signal (aluminium cans and can linings, closures, filter aids, additive carry-over) rather than a raw-material contaminant. Aluminium is a live cell here because canned formats are common and because a pH 2.5 to 3.8 ferment is an aggressive environment for a can lining; the tripwire is a packaging-integrity control as well as an ingredient control.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented process baseline escalates to a packaging, can-lining and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

Cr.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for a non-tea fermented beverage. The only sovereign chromium values reachable from this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada), which are water-utility instruments and not food law at all. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-steel equipment and process-water leaching screen, not as a health limit; the health-relevant species is addressed in the Cr-VI cell.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in a non-tea fermented beverage. At the pH of this product form (typically pH 2.5 to 3.8 after fermentation, with lactic, acetic, citric and malic acid and residual sugars present) Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by the organic acids, sugars, ascorbate and polyphenols present in the matrix, so a positive Cr(VI) result is an artifact of the total-chromium determination rather than a species present in the beverage as consumed. The reference-method basis for this determination is the in-house species arbitration at data/workbench/standards/2026-07-31-chromium-formula-adjudication.md, which found that the superseded ion-exchange plus electrothermal-AAS methods that generated the historical Cr(VI) values in liquid food matrices are not reproduced by the modern reference method: saraiva2021 (species-specific isotope dilution HPLC-ICP-MS, limit of quantification 0.049 ug/kg) quantified no Cr(VI) in any milk or formula sample while resolving Cr(III) and total chromium at single-digit ug/kg. That adjudication was drawn on a near-neutral aqueous food matrix; the acidic beverage matrices in this row are a more strongly reducing environment still, so the artifact conclusion carries a fortiori. The health-relevant species is controlled through the total-chromium cell and the reflex rule below, and this determination is a method finding, not an occurrence-derived value: no number is taken from it.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium is not a routine lot test. Total chromium (Cr cell) bounds any hexavalent fraction; a Cr(VI)-specific method (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted to the liquid matrix) is reflexed where the total-chromium screen is elevated AND the finished-product pH is above 5.0, and a confirmed detection blocks certification pending a process and equipment investigation.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food or beverage; every sovereign chromium value in a dietary or packaged-water basis is written for total chromium (US 21 CFR 165.110 chromium 100 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water 50 ug/kg). Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for a food or beverage.
